evidence.reason: The identity-less cleanup path queries the derived scope, but when `LoadState` is `not-found` it skips the ownership check and still unconditionally runs `systemctl --user stop derived_unit`. Because the unit name is derived only from the run id, and the code itself acknowledges that another workspace under the same user manager can own a same-named scope, a scope created between the query and the stop can be stopped without proving ownership. The post-stop check then sees that other scope inactive and treats it as success. This is an implementation error in the intended ownership protection; skipping the stop when the scope was absent is the smallest compatible repair.
